questions.q: How long should you wait after applying non-selective herbicide before starting site prep for sod?
questions.explanation: Waiting the labeled interval (usually 7-14 days) ensures the herbicide has translocated to roots and killed the target weeds. Rushing this step is the #1 cause of weeds returning in new sod.

questions.q: For a cool-season turf install, the target soil pH range is:
questions.explanation: Cool-season turf (fescue, bluegrass, ryegrass) prefers a slightly acidic to neutral soil around pH 6.0-7.0.

questions.q: How thick should compost amendment be tilled into heavy clay or pure sand soils?
questions.explanation: 3-4 cubic yards per 1000 square feet tilled into the top 4 inches gives measurable improvement in root penetration and moisture holding.

questions.q: When laying sod, joints between rows should be:
questions.explanation: Staggered joints (like brickwork) distribute stress and prevent long seam lines that dry out and show as yellow stripes.

questions.q: On a slope steeper than about one-in-six, sod should be laid:
choices: Perpendicular to the slope with the top edge staked
In small pieces to hold better
questions.explanation: Perpendicular to slope prevents sliding, and staking the top edge keeps the roll in place until roots knit into the soil.

questions.q: The most important watering event for new sod is:
questions.explanation: The first watering, applied immediately, presses roots against soil and prevents drying. A dry first hour can cost 20-30% of a roll's survival.

questions.q: During the first two weeks after install, warm-weather watering frequency should be:
questions.explanation: New sod has almost no root reach. Twice-daily light watering keeps the shallow root zone continuously moist without oversaturating.

questions.q: First mow of new sod should happen at:
questions.explanation: By 3-4 weeks, roots have knit firmly enough that mowing won't pull rolls up. Testing with a gentle tug on a corner is the field check.

questions.q: The one-third rule of mowing means:
choices: Never remove more than one third of leaf blade height in a single mowing
Water for one third of daylight hours
questions.explanation: Removing more than a third of the leaf blade in one mow stresses the grass and slows recovery. This rule applies to all turf, not just new sod.

questions.q: Yellow strips along sod roll edges within the first two weeks are a symptom of:
choices: Dry-out from gaps or seams not receiving water
questions.explanation: Yellow seam patterns are almost always a watering coverage issue — either gaps between rolls or watering that hits tops but not seams. Hand-watering seams for a week usually restores them.
